annotations.text:
ONBOARDING → PAYOFF

Four questions, then the verdict. The cushion screen is the whole product in one number — it now leads with 244 set at 78px instead of burying it in a tinted box.

Only SSC CGL has a real syllabus tree in data.js, so it is the only card showing hour counts. The other five need trees before they can show anything.

THE DAILY LOOP

What the prototype was thinnest on. Added: a real timeline rail with state-carrying nodes, a now-marker, and a day-progress bar that answers "am I on track today" before you read a single card.

Bottom nav replaces the two top tabs — thumb-reachable, and it makes room for Focus and You.

RECOVERY + PLATFORM

Rebalance reuses the exact choice-row component from the cushion screen, so "pick one of three" is one learned pattern, not two.

Right: the same Today screen adapted to iOS. Compare the header, the list treatment and the tab bar — that is the entire visual fork.

SYSTEM

Every value lifted from tokens.css rather than re-picked, so the CMP theme is a transcription job.

The fork table at the bottom is the part worth arguing about before any Kotlin gets written.
